title: Rollouts playbook — interactive flow for canary / A/B / traffic split with rollback affordances
creator: Leah Park
description:
Summary: Design an interactive, production-ready Rollouts UI inside Redwood Console that supports canary releases, A/B experiments, traffic-splitting across model variants, and safe rollback flows. The goal is to make progressive rollouts predictable for engineers and product owners: clearly show traffic allocation, expected latency/cost deltas, health signals, and an auditable timeline.

Goals and success metrics:
- Allow users to configure canary and A/B rollouts with percentage ramps and time-based schedules.
- Surface cost delta estimates and latency/throughput expectations for each variant before and during rollout.
- Provide one-click manual rollback and automated rollback policies based on configurable signals (errors, latency, quality regression).
- Make the experience discoverable and safe (confirmations, scaffolding, guardrails).
- Reduce rollout misconfiguration incidents by 50% in Q2 measured via support tickets and postmortems.

Scope of this ticket: interactive flow prototypes, annotated wireframes, copy recommendations, and review notes. This is the primary design artifact for the engineering implementation ticket (ENG-2590).

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- We propose a single Rollout Editor surface that adapts based on mode (Canary vs A/B). This avoids fragmentation in the console and reduces training overhead.
- Percentage slider + numeric input for traffic split — sliders are quick for coarse changes, inputs for exact percentages.
- Time-phased ramp vs step schedule — time-phased is default for safety; step schedules available for advanced users.
- Show a cost delta badge computed from the last 24h token distribution and model cost profile. This is an estimate only and labeled as such.
- Automatic rollback should be opt-in and limited to guardrails (e.g., error rate + latency). Full ML-quality regression triggers remain an advanced, server-side config.

Prototype notes: 
- Primary flow: Create Rollout -> Pick base model and variant(s) -> Choose mode (Canary/A-B) -> Configure traffic split and schedule -> Choose health signals and rollback triggers -> Preview -> Start rollout.
- Preview panel includes: current vs target traffic graph, expected cost delta, estimated 95th latency change, active health signals, and a simulated timeline.
- Live Rollout page: top banner with rollout progress, traffic donut chart, time-series of latency/error/throughput, cost burn vs baseline, and an audit timeline listing changes and operator actions.
- Rollback UX: prominent rollback button with two modes (quick rollback to previous pinned model OR custom rollback percentage), confirmation modal showing estimated impact and required approvals if the rollout is > 50% traffic.

Accessibility & copy: 
- Use clear, action-oriented microcopy for risky actions (e.g., "Start canary rollout — this will route X% traffic to Variant B").
- Ensure color + pattern coding for traffic doughnuts to be colorblind-safe.

Open questions for engineering and PM: 
- What is the minimum viable telemetry we can rely on for automated rollback? (SLOs provided by runtime team vs customer-configured metrics) — noted for ENG-1842.
- How to compute cost-delta accurately for multi-tenant Dedicated customers with committed discounts? Work with billing on the approximate model.

PRD (Confluence) — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Rollouts+Console+Playbook
Engineering ticket (implementation) — https://linear.redwood.ai/issue/ENG-2590
Design system components referenced — https://design.redwood.ai/components/traffic-slider

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity prototype of the full flow in Figma covering Create, Preview, Live rollout, and Rollback.
- Annotated handoff spec including API hooks required (traffic allocation API, rollout state, metrics endpoints) and a list of required telemetry signals.
- Design review complete with Eng/PM signoff and three usability test notes from internal playthrough.
updates: 2025-03-18: Initial draft of flows and wireframes completed. Shared with Priya and Marco for early feedback.

2025-03-19: Synchronized with runtime team (Marco Alvarez). Runtime cautioned that 5s latency probes are expensive on small Dedicated clusters; recommended sampling. Added note to telemetry requirements.
2025-03-20: PM feedback (Omar Haddad) requested a cost-delta badge and clear labeling when an estimate is only approximate. Added cost estimation UI with disclaimers.

2025-03-22: First high-fidelity prototype in Figma uploaded. Usability playthrough with two engineers + one solutions engineer; captured 3 action items (clarify schedule defaults, add explicit revert-to-pin option, surface API link for automation).
2025-03-24: Design review scheduled with Eng & PM. Received verbal approval on primary flow; Eng requested an expanded spec for automated rollback edge cases. Moving to In Review.
2025-03-25: Addressed design review comments; added explicit audit timeline UI and approval gating for rollouts above 50% traffic. Updated Figma and Confluence links.
